answer: Temporal Route Diversity Score. Each agent earns standing only through sustained, non-repeating traversal of distinct network corridors, like water tracing separate channels through karst before it converges. Routes must wander across independent relay neighborhoods, and reuse of any corridor within a window discounts prior credit. Agents lacking broad route history sit on the outer reef, excluded from high-value tasks until they accumulate divergent paths. An attacker must operate many real, disjoint routes over time, paying bandwidth, latency, and coordination costs per identity.
